display.purpose: Page title 'ore' on login. Rare; signals major page boundary.

headline.purpose: Component titles, major section headings. 'Infrastructure Status', 'Configuration Panel'.

title.purpose: Module names, card titles, form group headings.

body.purpose: Form labels, descriptions, helper text. Default text throughout UI. Line length 65–75ch.

label.purpose: Metadata, timestamps, status tags, form hints. Smallest interactive text.

mono.purpose: Terminal output, values, code references. Never antialiased for pixel-perfect legibility.

shadows.name: none
shadows.purpose: ore uses tonal layering, not shadows. All depth is communicated via background color and borders.

motion.name: standard-ease
motion.purpose: All state transitions (button hover, input focus, color changes). 200ms duration.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: Small screens (mobile). Not yet fully responsive; Phase 2+ work.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Bold action button. Plan, Apply, Save Config, and other primary CTAs. Hover to darker blue.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #2563eb; color: #f3f4f6; padding: 8px 16px; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; border: none; border-radius: 8px; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 200ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #1d4ed8; } .ds-btn-primary:active { background: #1d4ed8; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { background: #4b5563; color: #6b7280; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Subtle action button. Cancel, Close, or lower-priority actions. Hover shifts background.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { background: #374151; color: #f3f4f6; padding: 8px 16px; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; border: none; border-radius: 8px; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 200ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1); } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: #4b5563; } .ds-btn-secondary:active { background: #4b5563; } .ds-btn-secondary:disabled { background: #1f2937; color: #6b7280; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Standard form input. Focus border shifts to blue. Validation errors shown as red text below, not border color.
components.css: .ds-input { background: #374151; color: #f3f4f6; border: 1px solid #4b5563; padding: 8px 12px; font-size: 0.875rem; border-radius: 8px; transition: border-color 200ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1); } .ds-input:focus { outline: none; border-color: #2563eb; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #9ca3af; } .ds-input:disabled { background: #1f2937; color: #6b7280; border-color: #374151; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Card / Container
components.description: Content container. Tonal background, subtle border, rounded corners. Used for ConfigPanel, Terminal, MonitorDash, etc.
components.html:
Infrastructure Status

All systems operational
components.css: .ds-card { background: #1f2937; border: 1px solid #4b5563; border-radius: 8px; padding: 24px; } .ds-card-title { font-size: 1.125rem; font-weight: 600; color: #f3f4f6; margin: 0 0 16px 0; } .ds-card-text { font-size: 0.875rem; color: #d1d5db; line-height: 1.6; margin: 0; }

components.name: Module (Canvas Node)
components.description: Infrastructure module on canvas. 48×48px square, icon + label below. Color follows hierarchy (VPC bold, dependents muted).
components.css: .ds-module { width: 48px; height: 48px; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; border-radius: 4px; cursor: move; position: relative; transition: transform 200ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1); } .ds-module:hover { transform: scale(1.05); } .ds-module-icon { font-size: 24px; } .ds-module-label { position: absolute; bottom: -24px; left: 50%; transform: translateX(-50%); font-size: 0.75rem; color: #d1d5db; white-space: nowrap; font-weight: 500; } .ds-module-vpc { background: #2563eb; } .ds-module-ecs { background: #ea580c; } .ds-module-rds { background: #16a34a; } .ds-module-alb { background: #0891b2; }

components.name: Terminal Output Line
components.description: Colored output line in Terminal. Color reflects message type: green (success), red (error), yellow (warning), blue (info), gray (default).
components.html:
✓ VPC created successfully
Error: Invalid CIDR notation
Plan: 5 to add, 0 to change
components.css: .ds-terminal { background: #111827; border: 1px solid #374151; border-radius: 8px; padding: 16px; font-family: 'Monaco', 'Courier New', monospace; font-size: 0.75rem; line-height: 1.6; max-height: 400px; overflow-y: auto; } .ds-term-line { margin: 0; color: #d1d5db; } .ds-term-success { color: #4ade80; } .ds-term-error { color: #f87171; } .ds-term-warning { color: #facc15; } .ds-term-info { color: #60a5fa; }

components.name: Error Message
components.description: Inline validation error. Red text below input field. Shown on change; clears when corrected.

components.name: Success Toast
components.description: Success feedback message. Green background, subtle style. Appears for 3s after save/deploy.
components.css: .ds-success { background: #15803d; color: #dcfce7; padding: 12px 16px; border-radius: 8px; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; animation: fadeInOut 3s ease-out; } @keyframes fadeInOut { 0% { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(-8px); } 10% { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); } 90% { opacity: 1; } 100% { opacity: 0; } }

narrative.overview: ore's interface is a blueprint-focused design system inspired by how architects work: clear line weights, intentional hierarchy, visible relationships between components, and a restrained tonal palette that emphasizes information over decoration. Infrastructure engineers using ore should feel like they're designing something precise and intentional—each module placement, each configuration change, each deployment carries weight and is visible on the canvas. The system deliberately rejects SaaS dashboard clichés, gaming UI effects, and terminal envy. Instead, it provides a space where the infrastructure—not the interface—is the focus.
keyCharacteristics: Methodical and precise—every element has visual intent; nothing is decorative
Visual relationships matter—module dependencies shown via connectors; proximity conveys meaning
Trustworthy under pressure—errors are actionable; destructive operations require confirmation
Instant feedback—SSE streaming shows exactly what's happening in real time

rules.name: The Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: VPC always receives the primary accent color. All dependent modules receive desaturated, toned versions. This creates visual subordination: a glance at the canvas shows the infrastructure topology just from module color intensity.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: The primary accent color appears on ≤10% of any canvas (typically the VPC module and one primary CTA button). Its rarity is the point.

rules.name: The Tonal Depth Rule
rules.body: ore uses tonal layering, not shadow depth. Depth is communicated through background color shifts and stroke weight, never blur or drop shadows.

rules.name: The Trust Rule
rules.body: Validate early and show errors inline. Never prevent form submission with disabled buttons; instead, show a clear error message and let users attempt to save. Destructive operations require explicit confirmation.

rules.name: The Streaming Rule
rules.body: Terraform output streams live via SSE. Never buffer or hide progress. Real-time output builds trust.

dos: Do use the primary accent color (#2563eb) sparingly and intentionally.
Do express module relationships through color hierarchy: VPC bold, dependents desaturated.
Do show infrastructure state before offering actions.
Do use tonal layering (background color shifts) instead of shadows.
Do validate early and show errors inline (red text below fields).
Do stream terraform output in real time (SSE). Never buffer or hide progress.
Do require explicit confirmation for destructive operations (destroy, delete).
Do use consistent 8px spacing grid. Stick to the scale (8, 16, 24, 32px for padding).
donts: Don't use side-stripe borders (border-left or border-right > 1px) as colored accents on cards or alerts.
Don't use gradients (background or text). Status and hierarchy come from solid colors and weight.
Don't use glassmorphism, backdrop blur, or drop shadows as default effects.
Don't mix status colors with module colors. Red = state (error/alert), not module type.
Don't decorate inputs with icons unless the icon is functional.
Don't use animations for layout changes (don't animate CSS grid, flexbox, or position).
Don't hide errors behind loading spinners. Use SSE streaming to show real progress and real failures.
Don't SaaS-ify the interface: no hero metrics, no gradient overlays, no identical card grids.
Don't try to look like a CLI when a GUI is better. The terminal shows terraform output; the GUI shows infrastructure visually.
